claims.text: Reducing individual layer thickness in HEA multilayer coatings increases interface density.
The increased interface density provides more dislocation-pinning sites.
Interfaces in the refined multilayer act as effective barriers to dislocation glide.
Impeded dislocation motion reduces plastic deformation under sustained load.
Reducing individual layer thickness lowers the rate of time-dependent plastic deformation relative to thicker-layer coatings.
The reduced-layer-thickness coating is expected to have a lower creep strain rate than the baseline coating under identical conditions.
The reduced-layer-thickness coating may have a longer creep lifetime than the baseline coating.
The proposed effect applies when creep is dominated by dislocation-mediated plasticity.
The proposed effect may not apply when other failure mechanisms, such as oxidation at extreme temperatures, prevail.
The magnitude of creep-rate reduction depends on the extent of layer-thickness reduction.
The magnitude of creep-rate reduction depends on how dislocations interact with the specific interfaces in the HEA system.
